**Jennifer Joanna Aniston** (born February 11, 1969) is an American actress, producer and businesswoman. She rose to international fame for her role as Rachel Green on the television sitcom *Friends* from 1994 to 2004, for which she earned Primetime Emmy, Golden Globe, and Screen Actors Guild awards. Since her career progressed in the 1990s, she has become one of the world's highest-paid actresses.[1]


</fragment>
<fragment>
Depressed over her four unsuccessful television shows, Aniston approached Warren Littlefield at a Los Angeles gas station asking for reassurance. As the head of NBC entertainment, he encouraged her to continue acting, and a few months later helped cast her in *Friends*,[20][17] a sitcom set to debut on NBC's 1994–1995 fall lineup. The producer wanted Aniston to audition for the role of Monica Geller,[21] but Courteney Cox was deemed more suitable, and Aniston was cast as Rachel Green. She was also offered a spot as a featured player on *Saturday Night Live*, but turned it down in favor of *Friends*.[22] She played Rachel until the show ended in 2004, when Aniston took a 15-year hiatus from television save for occasional guest roles.

**Matthew Steven LeBlanc** (/ləˈblɒŋk/; born July 25, 1967) is an American actor. He garnered global recognition with his portrayal of Joey Tribbiani in the NBC sitcom *Friends* and in its spin-off series, *Joey*. For his work on *Friends*, LeBlanc received three nominations at the Primetime Emmy Awards. He has also starred as a fictionalized version of himself in *Episodes* (2011–2017), for which he won a Golden Globe Award and received four additional Emmy Award nominations. He co-hosted *Top Gear* from 2016 to 2019. From 2016 to 2020, he played patriarch Adam Burns in the CBS sitcom *Man with a Plan.*

**Jennifer Joanna Aniston** (born February 11, 1969) is an American actress, producer and businesswoman. She rose to international fame for her role as Rachel Green on the television sitcom *Friends* from 1994 to 2004, for which she earned Primetime Emmy, Golden Globe, and Screen Actors Guild awards. She was also offered a spot as a featured player on *Saturday Night Live*, but turned it down in favor of *Friends*.[22] She played Rachel until the show ended in 2004, when Aniston took a 15-year hiatus from television save for occasional guest roles.

- **Already Famous**: Cox was the most famous cast member when "Friends" began, having already been on the popular TV drama "Family Ties" for its entire run from 1982-1989.

- **Not the First Choice**: Kudrow was not the original actress cast as Phoebe. Another actress initially played the role in the pilot, but Kudrow replaced her for the series.
- **Comedy Background**: She had experience in improvisational comedy before landing this breakthrough role.

- **Soap Opera Experience**: Before "Friends," LeBlanc had appeared in several television series, including "TV 101," "Just the Ten of Us," and "Married... with Children" as Vinnie Verducci.

- **Struggling Actor Background**: Perry had been in a few failed television shows and was basically looking for the kind of steady work a network sitcom could provide.

- **First Actor Cast**: Schwimmer was actually the FIRST actor cast in the show and was specifically in the producers' minds when creating the character of Ross.
- **Established Theater Background**: He had a strong theater and academic background, having graduated from Northwestern University and co-founded a Chicago theater company.

- **David Schwimmer** had previously worked with one of the executive producers (Kevin S. Bright), which is why the character of Ross was written specifically with him in mind.
- The casting directors brought together actors with different backgrounds - from established sitcom stars (Cox) to struggling actors (Perry, Aniston) to theater-trained performers (Schwimmer) to character actors (LeBlanc, Kudrow).
- Their chemistry was discovered during the audition process rather than from pre-existing friendships.

The casting process, rather than pre-existing connections, was what brought them together and created television history.
